messages:
alex: ran quick heat-check across A100/H100/L40S for the new shadowed-attn variant. seq sweep 32/128/512, bsz 1/4/16. initial weirdness: H100 latency regressed at seq128 bsz1 vs A100 by ~18%.

maya: can you drop the raw numbers? which kernel variant exactly (flash, paged, fused)?

alex: test matrix: 
```
model: rwd/llamax-13b
kernels: flash_variants (flash_v2, shadowed_flash), paged_fused
gpus: [A100-40GB, H100-80GB, L40S-48GB]
seqs: [32,128,512]
bsz: [1,4,16]
prefetch_threshold: 24 -> candidate 40
```
key numbers (p50 latency ms per token, inferred from token rate):
```
A100 seq128 bsz1 flash_v2: 3.9 ms/token
H100 seq128 bsz1 flash_v2: 4.6 ms/token  <-- regressed
L40S seq128 bsz1 flash_v2: 5.1 ms/token
A100 seq128 bsz1 shadowed_flash: 3.7 ms/token
H100 seq128 bsz1 shadowed_flash: 4.1 ms/token
paged_fused (A100 seq512 bsz16): 2.9 ms/token  (good throughput)
```

ryan: interesting. H100 is usually faster. any memory-copy or kernel fallback detected?

alex: perf-bot trace attached inline (summarized):
```
perf-bot: hot functions: kernel_launch (44%), memcpy_async (18%), kv_page_miss_handler (12%), cuda_sync (9%)
note: H100 runs showed higher memcpy_async due to extra staging on seq128 bsz1 workload.
```

sam: kv_page_miss_handler at 12% is suspicious. is the KV cache paging threshold/affinity different on H100 config?

alex: yes — on H100 nodes we run a slightly different NUMA affinity pinning (to avoid bus contention on multi-socket hosts). that seems to interact with our KVCACHE page alignment and triggers more memcpy/staging.

maya: do we see the regression only at small batch sizes? what about bsz4/16?

alex: bsz4 reduces the gap: H100 flash_v2 seq128 bsz4 -> 1.9 ms/token vs A100 1.8 ms/token. at bsz16 H100 catches up. So it's small-batch sensitivity + KV page crossing.

ryan: action items?

alex: proposed triage plan: 1) run a focused bisect of the kernel selector heuristic when seq_len in [64,192] for bsz=1 to reproduce locally; 2) force prefetch_threshold=40 on H100 runs to see if memcpy_async drops; 3) add a brief microbench that toggles KV page alignment to see change in kv_page_miss_handler rate.

maya: sounds good. can you paste the run command so QE can reproduce?

alex: run command we used:
```
./bench/run_attention.sh --model rwd/llamax-13b --kernel shadowed_flash --gpu H100 --seq 128 --bsz 1 --prefetch 24 --trace perf
```

perf-bot: perf summary uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/3333210000-shadowed-heatcheck (flamegraph + nvprof) :robot_face:

sam: quick note — when you force prefetch->40 last week, we saw slight token-quality deviation for a tiny prompt subset. keep evals in the loop before rolling to prod.

alex: acknowledged. will run eval-run (regression prompt set) in parallel and tag results.

maya: ok please post the focused bisect thread when you have results. if KV alignment is root cause we should consider heuristic: prefer contiguous kv pages for small-batch low-seq requests.

ryan: +1. also add flamegraph snapshot to the ticket so infra can check PCIe link util and NUMA rules.

alex: creating ticket: INF-4521, will include commands, perf links, and initial numbers. pinging @sam for evaluation checklist.

perf-bot: deploy-notify: canary agents scheduled to run the forced-prefetch variant at 3333211800 (ETA 30m).

maya: thanks — nice quick triage. :thumbsup:
